raw:
{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging", "note": "Kid is now caught between loyalty to parent and standing with teammates who saw the parent go around the coach." },
  "read": "The player knows the email happened, which means they know their parent fought a battle they didn't win themselves — that's embarrassing and it undercuts their status on this team. They may act defensive or distant, or overcorrect by trying too hard, because they feel like they're being seen as someone who needs a parent to advocate for them instead of earning it on their own.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Call the parent out, make the kid own the situation publicly, or quietly punish them with even less playing time — all of which shame the kid for something they may not have controlled and blow up the relationship." },
  "mentorMove": "Separate the kid from the parent's action. Go to them first, privately, before it festers — acknowledge the awkward situation with zero heat, restate the standard clearly, and give them a concrete path to earn what they want.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The starting spot is earned by what happens at practice and on film, full stop — the email changes nothing about that bar.",
    "You're not adjusting the depth chart in response to outside pressure, and the player needs to hear you say that plainly so they know the standard is real and fair."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "Open the door to a honest conversation about what the player themselves thinks they need more of — maybe they've been wanting to say something and didn't know how.",
    "Give them a specific, achievable target to focus on this week so they leave the conversation with agency, not just a verdict."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, got a minute? Come walk with me. I'm not bringing this up to make it weird — I just don't want something hanging between us that we haven't talked about." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "I know there was an email. I'm not asking you to answer for that — that's between your folks and me. What I do want to know is: how are you feeling about where things stand for you on this team right now? What do you think is going on?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here's what I see: you've got real ability, and there are two or three specific things that are the gap right now between where you are and where you want to be. Let's actually name them. I'd rather you and I talk about that directly than have it go any other route." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I hold every player on this team to a high standard — that's not going away. And I'm telling you straight: I think you can get there. That's why I'm having this conversation with you instead of just moving on. Work those two things we just named, and you give me something real to evaluate. That's the deal, and it's the same deal everybody else has." }
  ],
  "longGame": "If this player sees that you came to them directly, held the standard, and gave them a real path — rather than either caving or icing them out — you build the kind of trust that makes them run through a wall for you. The parent situation becomes a moment that actually strengthened the relationship instead of poisoning it."
}
situation: A player's parent emailed me arguing their kid should be starting, and the kid clearly knows about the email.
